title: The small pro-étale site
statement:
Let $X$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme]. The objects of $X_{\mathrm{proét}}$ are weakly étale $X$-schemes [sk-def-pe-morphisms],
with all $X$-morphisms as arrows (these are weakly étale by
[sk-lem-pe-weakly-etale-stability]). A family $\{U_i\to U\}_{i\in I}$ is a covering if it
is an fpqc covering. Explicitly, for every affine open $W\subset U$ there must be finitely
many indices $i_1,\ldots,i_m$ and affine opens $V_j\subset U_{i_j}\times_UW$ with

$$
W=\bigcup_{j=1}^m\operatorname{image}(V_j\to W).
$$

The indices may depend on $W$; no finiteness of $I$ is required. Equivalently one may use
finitely many quasi-compact opens above each $W$. The fpqc covering condition is [def-weil-pbc-fpqc-covering].

The finite refinement condition is part of the topology; a jointly surjective family
without it is not a covering. For an affine target every cover refines to a finite affine
cover, whose disjoint union is affine and faithfully flat over the target. Ordinary étale
and Zariski covers are pro-étale covers: flat maps locally of finite presentation are open,
so quasi-compactness gives the required finite refinements (Stacks, Tag 098B).

mathlib_match.how: Exact definition, with the explanatory clauses supplied by the following Mathlib declarations (all line numbers read in the pinned source). Objects and all X-morphisms: Scheme.ProEt (Sites/Proetale.lean:100), defined as MorphismProperty.Over @WeaklyEtale top X; arrows are weakly etale by AlgebraicGeometry.WeaklyEtale.of_comp (Morphisms/WeaklyEtale.lean:117), using the equation of an over-morphism and the two object instances. Coverings and topology: Scheme.proetalePrecoverage (Sites/Proetale.lean:52), Scheme.ProEt.precoverage (:151), and Scheme.ProEt.topology (:156); the first is propQCPrecoverage @WeaklyEtale, hence the jointly surjective weakly etale families satisfying QuasiCompactCover. QuasiCompactCover (Cover/QuasiCompact.lean:38) defines the finite quasi-compact-open condition; QuasiCompactCover.exists_isAffineOpen_of_isCompact (:60), specialized to an affine open W using its isCompact instance, supplies exactly the finite affine refinement. Conversely affine opens are quasi-compact; when an index repeats, replace its finitely many selected opens by their finite union, which is again quasi-compact and open. Equality of the union of images with W puts each selected open inside the inverse-image open of W, identified with the open base change. QuasiCompactCover.exists_hom (:183), with P = WeaklyEtale and the affine target, supplies a finite affine covering refinement; its required compact-target instance is Scheme.compactSpace_of_isAffine (AffineScheme.lean:561), and its open-immersion stability instance is IsZariskiLocalAtSource.respectsLeft_isOpenImmersion (Morphisms/Basic.lean:261), using the WeaklyEtale source-locality instance (Morphisms/WeaklyEtale.lean:80). The instance for a finite AffineCover of an affine scheme (Cover/QuasiCompact.lean:148, using QuasiCompactCover.of_finite at :140) supplies QuasiCompactCover for this refinement, so it is a pro-etale cover, not merely a jointly surjective weakly etale family. The finite coproduct is affine by the IsAffine (Sigma g) instance (Limits.lean:651); its map is flat by the Flat (Sigma.desc f) instance (Morphisms/Flat.lean:110), with component flatness inferred from weak etaleness, and surjective by AlgebraicGeometry.Surjective.sigmaDesc_of_union_range_eq_univ (Morphisms/UnderlyingMap.lean:116), applied to the covering image equality. These are the affine faithfully flat and finite-union clauses; Fin n is Small and Finite, including n = 0. Etale covers: Scheme.etalePrecoverage_le_proetalePrecoverage (Sites/Proetale.lean:72). Zariski covers: Scheme.zariskiPrecoverage_le_propQCPrecoverage (Sites/QuasiCompact.lean:125), specialized to P = WeaklyEtale; ContainsIdentities and IsZariskiLocalAtSource are the existing WeaklyEtale instances (Morphisms/WeaklyEtale.lean:66 and :80). The stated openness explanation is the instance AlgebraicGeometry.UniversallyOpen.of_flat (Morphisms/UniversallyOpen.lean:147), followed by Scheme.Hom.isOpenMap (:48). No additional quasi-separatedness, quasi-compactness of X, or finite indexing hypothesis is introduced.
